Now we are merging two PDDL domains into one domain. Please help judge whether two PDDL operators are equivalent.

domain_1:
    action in domain_1: (:action allow_woe_to_ride_on_shoulder :parameters (?poor ?woe - entity ?loc - location) :precondition (and (at ?poor ?loc) (at ?woe ?loc) (has_fatigue ?poor)) :effect (woe_on_shoulder ?woe ?poor))
    predicates explaination in domain_1: {'(at ?e - entity ?l - location)': "relation 'at' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?l is a location; used as precondition of stay_for_banquet, precondition of bow_to_guests, precondition of sing_cheerful_song, precondition of encounter_bitter_woe, precondition of make_sign_of_cross, precondition of allow_woe_to_ride_on_shoulder, precondition of spend_money_on_drink, precondition of take_gold_pot_and_hide", '(has_fatigue ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'has fatigue'; used as effect of perform_work_for_rich_brother, effect of encounter_bitter_woe, effect of make_sign_of_cross, precondition of allow_woe_to_ride_on_shoulder, effect of accept_woe_as_burden", '(woe_on_shoulder ?monster - entity ?carrier - entity)': "relation 'woe on shoulder' holds; arguments: ?monster is a entity, ?carrier is a entity; used as effect of allow_woe_to_ride_on_shoulder, precondition of hide_woe_under_stone, effect of hide_woe_under_stone, effect of rich_brother_attempt_to_move_stone, precondition of accept_woe_as_burden"}

domain_2:
    action in domain_2: (:action travel_by_leaf_boat_under_pond :parameters (?n - entity ?b - item ?palace ?pond - location) :precondition (and (stairs_descended ?n) (boat_available ?b ?pond)) :effect (at ?n ?palace))
    predicates explaination in domain_2: {'(at ?e - entity ?l - location)': "relation 'at' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?l is a location; used as precondition of travel_to_trysting_place, effect of travel_to_trysting_place, precondition of hear_tapping_on_beech, effect of approach_beech_tree, precondition of activate_beech, effect of travel_by_leaf_boat_under_pond, precondition of witness_queen_birthday_ceremony, precondition of receive_queen_kiss", '(boat_available ?b - item ?l - location)': "relation 'boat available' holds; arguments: ?b is a item, ?l is a location; used as precondition of travel_by_leaf_boat_under_pond", '(stairs_descended ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'stairs descended'; used as effect of enter_tree_and_descend_stairs, precondition of travel_by_leaf_boat_under_pond"}

Please judge whether the two operators can be merged into one action based on following rules:
(1) If the two actions have the same name, they MUST be merged into one action;
(2) If the two actions are semantically equivalent (although they may differ in preconditions and effects), merge them. Genrally, you need to union their preconditions and effects.
(3) Note that do NOT merge two actions if the logic becomes more complex after merging. For example, do NOT use "or", "when" to union two actions (about their preconditions and effects). Namely NOT too general. 
(4) Do NOT invent any predicate.
(5) If you decide to merge two actions. You can invent new action name. But the new name must be reasonable according to the whole predicates in the action.
    For example: if the action expresses the meaning of "pick some object from drawer" according to the predicates in preconditions and effects, just name it like "pick_from_drawer", instead of "pick_from_container", etc.
(6) Keep the given PDDL style. Please use PDDL 1.0 and do NOT use Conditional Effects like "when", etc.
(7) Note the number of brackets in the PDDL format.

Your output should include four part:
(1) reasoning: your analysis process;
(2) merge_flag: whether the two operators can be merged into one;
(3) new_operator_name: if equivalent, output the new operator name (in one of the given operator or a new invented operator).
(4) new_operator: if equivalent, output the new operator in PDDL format.

If "merge_flag" is false, the "new_operator_name" and "new_operator" parts are null.

Your output should be in JSON format like below:
{
    "reasoning": "your analysis process",
    "merge_flag": true,
    "new_operator_name": "open_door",
    "new_operator": "(:action open_door \n :parameters (?r ?d) \n :precondition (and (hand_free ?r)) \n :effect (and (is_open ?d)))"
}

Do NOT output any strange symbols like "\".

These two actions have completely different meanings and preconditions. They cannot be merged into one action.
